newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Red Cross rejects military protection for workers.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross rejects military protection for workers.

text.p: The head of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Monday it has rejected the idea of placing itself under military protection after the killing of six of its workers in Chechnya last year.

"In view of such barbaric acts, the question may be asked whether humanitarian organisations have any choice but to place their operations under military protection," ICRC President Cornelio Sommaruga said.

He said the question was raised after five ICRC nurses and a delegate were killed in their sleep by gunmen in December in Chechnya, where Russian troops and local guerrillas were engaged in a drawn-out conflict.
Three other ICRC workers were slain in an attack in Burundi in June while medical staff and U.N. human rights monitors were recently murdered in Rwanda in early February.

Sommaruga told a three-day conference on Humanitarian Action and Peace-keeping Operations that the ICRC could not use military protection because it would become ineffective in giving humanitarian assistance.

"Indeed, if we were to resort to such measures on a more general scale, humanitarian action would lose the neutrality and impartiality it must preserve in order to be able to operate in aid of all victims," he said.
But he added that using armed guards to protect ICRC premises against banditry had become unevoidable in some cases.

Sommaruga said the threat of using force to allow humanitarian work could eventually jeopardise the work of groups like the ICRC since the threat of military action "cannot be maintained indefinitely".
